A_target.statement:
Let $p, q > 1$ with $\dfrac 1 p + \dfrac 1 q = 1$, and $a, b \ge 0$.
Then:
:$a b \le \dfrac {a^p} p + \dfrac {b^q} q$

B_source.statement:
Let $x, y \in \R_{>0}$ and $t \in \closedint 0 1$.
Then, as $\ln$ is [[Definition:Concave Real Function|concave]]:
:$\map \ln {t x + \paren {1 - t} y} \ge t \ln x + \paren {1 - t} \ln y$

object_map.reformulation: Take logarithms, so the product ab becomes a weighted average of ln a^p and ln b^q.

validity_conditions: a and b must be strictly positive for the logarithms to exist; the case ab = 0 is trivial.
The conjugacy 1/p + 1/q = 1 is exactly what makes the weights a convex combination.
proof_plan: If $a = 0$ or $b = 0$ the result is immediate, so let $a, b > 0$.

Apply the source result with $x = a^p$, $y = b^q$ and $t = \dfrac 1 p$, so that $1 - t = \dfrac 1 q$:
:$\map \ln {\dfrac {a^p} p + \dfrac {b^q} q} \ge \dfrac 1 p \map \ln {a^p} + \dfrac 1 q \map \ln {b^q}$

By [[Logarithm of Power]] and [[Sum of Logarithms]], the right hand side is:
:$\ln a + \ln b = \map \ln {a b}$

As $\exp$ is [[Definition:Strictly Increasing Real Function|strictly increasing]]:
:$a b \le \dfrac {a^p} p + \dfrac {b^q} q$
which is [[Young's Inequality for Products]].
{{qed}}
